summary.p: Build @tinyactors/node again from scratch as one Node-API addon in C, to the "done means" of the Python binding's step 8.4, then through the rest of 8.5 that the Python binding has already walked (telemetry, hibernation, migration, snapshots, invoked services, W3C, the transport, packaging). The Python binding is the map: its rulebook, its mapping table, its loop and its review findings are reused as decisions already made; only what differs in Node-API, in JavaScript or between Node.js and Bun is decided again.

The two hard parts are the native "ecmascript" datamodel in the application's own engine (one realm, no parser API, no per-session global object) and the event loop (no loop object to hold, only setImmediate and setTimeout called from C). Everything else is a translation of tinyactors-cpython/src file by file.

fact.claim: A host belongs to the Node-API environment (the main thread or one worker) that made it; a napi_value or napi_ref means nothing in another environment, so the addon's state is instance data or on the Host.
fact.evidence: tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, "No mutable globals", "One thread per host"; tinyactors-core/docs/bindings.md section 5, "One thread".

fact.claim: The loop is take, handle, ack, run, written as the binding's drain and turn; one drain at a time, no nested drain, a run refused while a batch is open.

Every send that leaves a segment without a delay parks its sender until the host decides it: at once for a send it delivers itself (another segment), at the ack of the batch for a send it hands out (an I/O processor, a service, the transport). "sync" I/O processors are gone. An answer or failure given in the handler, before the ack, is what the sender sees when it goes on; one given later arrives as an ordinary event.

Sends to another system's address are TA_EFFECT_SEND with io_processor 0 (the SCXML processor; I/O processors are numbered as _ioprocessors numbers them, the config's from 1), for a host-level transport handler that needs no config; without one the binding fails each such send. A send between systems is one message in two halves: the outgoing half a value holding ta_event_in's fields (Python's send.message), the incoming half the input that takes it unchanged (host.send(message)); a failure is an explicit input (host.fail(address, sendid)); target and origin are the language's address value, whose parts ta_address_parse reads. Peers, envelopes and PEER/PEER_ERROR are gone.
fact.evidence: commits f4c2819, bf0b8a1 ("one numbering of I/O processors"), f53ae02 (ADR 0017 decisions 4 and 5); tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/host.h:287-289; tinyactors-core/docs/bindings.md section 9, "Other systems".

fact.claim: Node's two datamodels are both named "ecmascript": the native one and quickjs. A host's environment holds only one of them, because core matches a chart's datamodel attribute against the vtable's name; the suite's adapter puts only the one asked for in the host.
fact.evidence: tinyactors-test/docs/driver.md, "The chart language" (lines 72-82); bindings.md section 8, "A datamodel is chosen by name".

fact.claim: The datamodel vtable is the only call out of core; its entries run inside ta_host_run, which is one native call from JavaScript, and some (release, destroy) run outside a run too: at the ack, in posts and in ta_host_free.
fact.evidence: tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/datamodel.h (ta_datamodel_call: environment NULL outside a step); bindings.md sections 5 and 8.

fact.claim: quickjs's shared realm compiles each expression once per chart as function(__s){with(__s){return (function(){'use strict'; ...})}}: a sloppy outer function holding the with, a strict inner one, so identifiers resolve to the session's scope and an undeclared assignment throws. Charts whose scripts declare top-level names stay isolated, and the declared names are asked of the engine.

SCXML B.2, as quickjs implements it: <content> and <data> text is JSON if it parses, a minimal XML DOM if it is XML, else a space-normalized string. The DOM is a JavaScript prelude inside the quickjs datamodel, not a public function.

Every one of the 191 automatic W3C tests applies to a native ECMAScript datamodel: the B.2 tests (444 to 578, skipped for Python) name datamodel="ecmascript", and 452 declares a function in a top-level <script>, 557 and 561 need the XML DOM.

What the first addon left stands: mise/napi.rb (the build with Toolchain::Target.host and #plugin, the gate, the runtimes), the tasks build, conform, lint, test, pack (aborts), the eight ast-grep rules with tests, test/harness.mjs, an empty docs/api-map.md, and an index.mjs that throws.

The Python binding has done everything 8.5 asks of a binding except examples and its first release (0.1.0 is tagged): M1 to M4 on both datamodels, W3C 191/191 on quickjs and 171/171 native, the API review applied, packaging built.
fact.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/ROADMAP.md, opening paragraph and "The W3C suite, M2"; commit 43b8207 (release v0.1.0).

roles.first: The application developer writing JavaScript on Node.js or Bun: chart logic in the application's own ECMAScript engine, a Host on the runtime's event loop, values that are JavaScript values.
roles.then: The binding author (held to the guide by the suite), the maintainers (one suite, two bindings compared file by file), the capacity planner (a measured cost per actor on V8 and JavaScriptCore beside quickjs), the operator and the observability backend (telemetry through the application's exporter).
roles.answers: Core already answers every behavioural question; the Python binding already answers every shape question that is not about JavaScript. This plan adds no behaviour: each API item is a row of docs/api-map.md over a core function, method or effect.

pays.cost: One napi_call_function per expression the chart evaluates on the native datamodel, a handle scope per vtable entry; no CBOR on the native datamodel's path (payloads are rows holding a napi_ref); CBOR only toward quickjs.
A scope object with the chart's <data> ids, a session row in ta_table, and the last _event; measured in phase 1 step 9, not estimated here.
The Python binding's surface in JavaScript names (section api), plus one choice Python does not have: which ECMAScript datamodel a host runs (decision d-datamodel).
Nothing new for the Python binding; every request to core this plan files is checked against both bindings.

out-of-scope.item: The convenience layer (a mapping of name to text, spawn by name, a chart builder, a directory resolver): later, in JavaScript, over the addon only.
Run-time fetching through TA_EFFECT_REQUEST: answered in C with TA_ERROR_INVALID until the root roadmap decides it.
The browser package and Deno: root ROADMAP.md, "Decided later".
A JSON-RPC transport, a raw post, a synchronous request, subscriptions: refused by ADR 0012.

studied.source: The rulebook: the API, the loop and its driver table, thin views and records, the binding's memory, the "python" datamodel, the C rules, the tests the suite cannot see.

The plan as it ran: the bootstrap, steps 1 to 9, the decisions made in 8.4, the memory and throughput review, then telemetry, hibernation, migration, snapshots, services, W3C, the API review and packaging, each with what its review found.
Every Python API item with its core: the inventory this plan translates.
The drain with its bound and batch flag, the turn with its bound of 64 runs, the asyncio driver's settle, the SimulatedClock holding its hosts weakly.
The adapter: the datamodel names, typed methods by name, the resolver of a call's documents.
The Node rulebook as written before 8.5, partly stale (section rulebook).
The step's done means and how the session works.
The guide: sections 3 (loop), 4 (effects), 5 (reentrancy), 6 (memory, thin views), 8 (datamodels), 9 (values, other systems), 10 (typed methods).
The vtable a native datamodel fills.
quickjs's realms, the compiled shape, the B.2 content rules, the declaration analysis.
The adapter's protocol, the datamodel names and the chart language.

decision.question: Which ECMAScript datamodel does a host run, since both are named "ecmascript" and a host can hold only one?
decision.option: A Host option, datamodel: "native" | "quickjs", default "native": the environment's datamodel list holds that one.
Only the native one in the API; quickjs only in the adapter.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): quickjs is the sandboxed ECMAScript datamodel; the native datamodel uses the application's JavaScript objects directly in its own engine, as the "python" datamodel uses Python's, and a host that names no datamodel gets the native one ("Native may be the default. Actually, it's what most people will expect.", an exception the maintainer makes to "no defaults of our own"). Both pass the same suite. The option names an environment entry, which is core's (environment->datamodels). quickjs as a sandbox needs its limits passed through (ta_datamodel_ecmascript_config: max_ops, memory_limit, the realm), which Python does not expose.

decision.question: How does a handler that finishes later (an async function, a function returning a promise) get a send that outlives the ack?
decision.option: Every handler gets a thin view; when the handler returns a thenable, the addon materializes that view in place before the ack (every field converted into its cache, answer and fail no longer checking the ack count) and fails the send if the promise rejects before an answer.
Decide at registration, as Python does (Object.prototype.toString gives "[object AsyncFunction]"): async functions get a record, others a view.
decision.recommendation: In JavaScript a plain function that returns a promise is as common as an async function, and registration-time detection misses it. Materializing at the return is still "before the ack, at a point the binding names" (bindings.md section 6), and a handler that returns nothing pays nothing. The rules that make it sound: the view records whether it was answered or failed, so a later rejection fails only an unanswered send; reading .then is user code inside the drain, allowed like any handler's; a view kept and used from a callback the handler did not return (a setTimeout) is stale and throws there, and its send is neither answered nor failed, as in Python; a rejection after its turn is reported as decision d-errors says. Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16: "the send rule is okay").
decision.evidence: s-async: the tag is "[object AsyncFunction]" in node 22.22.0 and bun 1.4.2, so at-registration is possible; it does not see a promise-returning plain function.

decision.question: The unit of time at the API: milliseconds or seconds?
decision.option: Milliseconds (a number), as setTimeout, Date.now() and xstate's SimulatedClock.increment(ms) use; nextDeadline, migrate's timeout, increment, now.
Seconds, as Python's API review chose.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16: "milliseconds make sense because that's what JavaScript programmers expect"): a deliberate difference from Python's seconds, each binding using its language's unit. Ticks stay inside the addon.
decision.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/ROADMAP.md, "The API review": "Seconds at every boundary"; tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, "A simulated clock".

decision.question: When does the event loop drive a host?
decision.option: Always, and only it: the host works on the runtime's event loop with nothing for the programmer to choose or start. An input from outside a turn schedules one turn with setImmediate; a turn that yields schedules the next; an idle turn arms one setTimeout at the deadline, ref'd while it is pending. There is no synchronous driver in the API.
Only once idle() was awaited, as Python attaches asyncio's loop at the first idle().
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): "Python had a choice between using an event loop and not using an event loop, but obviously in Node, this is not a thing. So it should work transparently with the event loop from the perspective of a JavaScript programmer." await host.idle() stays as a promise that settles when the host is next idle (for tests and an orderly shutdown); it observes the loop's turns and drives nothing. setImmediate, not a microtask, so I/O runs between turns. What follows, for the README: an open host with a pending deadline (a <send delay="1h">) keeps the process alive until it or close(), and its timer holds the Host, so it is not collected before; close() from a handler is deferred to the end of the turn.
decision.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/src/loop.c, ta_python_loop_schedule (returns when host->loop is None); bindings.md section 3, "Not every program has an event loop" (Node's always has one) and "Bound each turn".

decision.question: The shape of a typed method.
decision.option: method(params, onResult, onError?): params an object passed to core as given.
method(onResult, onError?, params?), Python's order.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16: "Params first is fine"): host.actorState({session}, onResult, onError) in the direct layer, returning nothing, as ADR 0012 decision 3 has it; a method without params takes undefined or {} first; onError is never a param for core. A promise form is the convenience layer's (decision d-promises).

decision.question: What is Compiled.image?
decision.option: A Uint8Array over an external ArrayBuffer on ta_compile_image's bytes, detached at close().
One copy into a Buffer (napi_create_buffer_copy), made on first read and cached; close() calls ta_compile_free and the copy stays the application's.
decision.recommendation: The repository already refuted a detached external buffer for the host's outputs, and the same readers reach an image: transfer() moves the bytes out of the detach's reach, Bun's fs.promises.writeFile reads the old pointer after the detach, a queued socket write loses its bytes, and Node-API requires an external buffer to stay valid until its finalizer runs. An image is copied by addImage anyway and is a few kilobytes; one more copy, only when read, buys a value that is safe everywhere.
decision.evidence: tinyactors-core/docs/boundary.md section 7, "Decided (2026-10-14): one copy, in the binding" and its refuted alternative; .agents/skills/boundary-design, "Ideas already rejected".
s-napi: the detach itself works in both runtimes; it does not end the readers above.

decision.question: The scoped form of a Host and a Compiled.
decision.option: close() plus [Symbol.dispose] (and [Symbol.asyncDispose] on Host, which awaits the promises of the last take's handlers), so using and await using work where the runtime parses them.
close() only.
decision.recommendation: Symbol.dispose and Symbol.asyncDispose exist in node 22 and bun, so the methods work and using works wherever the runtime parses it: bun 1.4 does, node 22 does not (spike s-js, corrected). The README promises close() and the symbols, not using, on the oldest Node the package claims.
decision.evidence: s-js (corrected): both symbols exist in both runtimes; node v22.22.0 and v22.23.3 answer "SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'x'" for a using declaration, bun parses it.

decision.question: Where does the native datamodel evaluate a chart, and what does it do with a <script>'s top-level declarations (var, function, let, const, class), which SCXML makes the session's global variables (W3C 452)?
decision.option: Contexts of node:vm (through process.getBuiltinModule), never the application's realm: one shared context for the charts that declare nothing, each session a scope object inside it; a context per session only for a chart whose scripts declare top-level names, where a script runs as global code and closures work. Whether a chart declares is asked of the engine at chart_attach (the script after throw 0; in a scratch context: the global's new names, and a second run's redeclaration error for let, const and class); the addon parses no JavaScript.
Refuse top-level declarations on the native datamodel, and skip W3C 452 there.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): "we can just pass Node.js VM objects if we really need to, a different global context ... I want to avoid having to parse JavaScript at runtime if possible", and "sharing per host is okay": one shared context per host's native datamodel, so every chart's values are of one realm, and a context per session only for a chart whose scripts declare top-level names (143 KB on node, 60 KB on bun, spike s-vm), which a chart's author chooses by writing var in a script. Pre-declaring names and copying bindings out stays rejected (closures).
decision.evidence: s-vm: declarations found by the engine in both runtimes (count and inc; b, c, D in their temporal dead zone); a shared context evaluates a session's scope; a per-session context keeps a closure over its var (count 2); the application's globalThis untouched; an application array inside a chart's context is not instanceof Array (Array.isArray is true).
datamodel_ecmascript.h:16-27 (quickjs's own rule, shared realm and isolated sessions, which this mirrors in Node's engine without sharing code with it).

decision.question: Where does the native datamodel's XML DOM for B.2 content (W3C 557, 561) come from, Node and Bun having no DOMParser?
decision.option: The project's XML library, txml (tinyxml/include/txml.c, freestanding, allocating through the allocator it is given), compiled into the addon: the content parsed in C and the DOM built as JavaScript objects with Node-API (nodeType, nodeName, childNodes, attributes, textContent, getElementsByTagName), the methods on one shared prototype in the datamodel's context.
A request to core for quickjs's prelude.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): the quickjs and native datamodels are completely separate, and the bindings may use the project's XML library where the runtime has no XML. The request r-dom is withdrawn. The addon's layer lint lets src/datamodel/ call txml_*; the build compiles txml's amalgamation; the test task's sources list tinyxml's.
decision.evidence: tinyxml/README.md ("freestanding XML reader and writer in C ... no C library, allocates only through an embedder-supplied allocator"); tinyxml/include/txml.c, txml.h.

decision.question: Where does an error go that the event loop's turn raises (a handler threw, a reply's error had no onError, a fault, an exhausted pool), or that a handler's promise rejects after its turn, when no idle() waits?
decision.option: Keep it for the next idle(), as Python's asyncio driver does.

Reject every waiting idle(); with none waiting, throw it from the turn's callback (after the timer is armed again, or the host stalls), and let a late rejection stay unhandled, so the runtime reports it as any uncaught error or unhandled rejection.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16: "you can raise errors"). There is no driver call to raise an error from (d-drive), so the turn rejects every waiting idle() and, with none waiting, throws from its callback after re-arming the timer; a late rejection stays unhandled. The README says that a handler's bug ends the process by default in Node unless the application handles uncaughtException or unhandledRejection (Bun's default unverified).
decision.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/src/loop.c:328-356 (ta_python_loop_settle: "nobody waits: the next idle() raises it"), :369-382 (the timer re-armed before the settle).

decision.question: What does SimulatedClock.increment(ms) do, now that there is no synchronous driver?
decision.option: It moves the clock and schedules a turn on every host made with it, like any input; a test awaits host.idle() to see what ran.
It turns every such host until idle before it returns, as xstate's and Python's do.
decision.recommendation: The decided rule (d-drive) has one driver, the event loop; a synchronous turn inside increment would be a second one, and would run handlers (and their promises' first steps) inside the caller's stack. The cost is one await in a test: clock.increment(1000); await host.idle(). Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): "Your clock proposal makes sense."
decision.evidence: bindings.md section 3, "A caller's own clock"; tinyactors-cpython/src/loop.c, ta_python_clock_increment.

decision.question: What is an address in JavaScript, now that the guide asks every binding for an address value with its system, session and name (f53ae02)?
decision.option: Python's shape (tinyactors-cpython/src/value_types.c): an immutable Address whose parts are read by core's parser on each access, .text, .system, .session (a bigint), .name (ta_address_parse, ta_address_name_decode), undefined for a part the text lacks; it is send.origin, the transport's send.target and their fields in send.message; host.send and host.fail take an Address or a string. toString() gives the text, so it prints and joins strings as the address.
Strings everywhere, with a function over the same parser.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16: "check what Python is doing"): the value is core's parser behind a JavaScript type, so no application or binding parses the grammar, and the two bindings have the same API. Inside event data an actor reference stays its address string: Node's datamodels are both ECMAScript, which has no reference type (values.txt, "ECMAScript: an actor reference is its address"; decided 2026-10-12), so tag 32 is still read as text there and never written.
decision.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/src/value_types.c:80-123; tinyactors-cpython/docs/api-map.md, rows Address.system, send.message; tinyactors-core/include/tinyactors/address.h; bindings.md section 9.

decision.question: May the native datamodel share code or text with quickjs's?
decision.option: No: the two ECMAScript datamodels are completely separate; they meet only in the suite they both pass.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): "the QuickJS model and the Node.js model, they have to be completely separate." So no request to core for quickjs's internals (r-declarations and r-dom withdrawn); the native datamodel asks its own engine and uses txml.

decision.question: How is the package layered?
decision.option: As Python's: the addon is the direct layer and mirrors core's API more or less one to one (compileCharts is ta_compile_charts, chart is ta_host_chart, spawn takes the reference chart returns, addImage returns the segment), every item a row of docs/api-map.md; a convenience layer in JavaScript (an image from a name-to-text mapping, spawn by chart name, a chart builder over ta_xml_writer, a directory resolver) comes later, calls only the direct layer, and adds shapes, never behaviour. index.mjs loads the addon and re-exports it, nothing else, until then.
decision.recommendation: Decided for both bindings (2026-10-13; bindings.md section 1, "Two layers"; tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, "Layers and the resolver"), confirmed by the maintainer for this plan (2026-10-16). The direct layer's completeness is checked, not assumed: step p0-inventory goes through every public header, as bindings.md section 2 asks, and the API review then reads the inventory as Python's did (it added compile_system and actor_by_name, and left ta_host_segment_count out).
decision.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/AGENTS.md, "Layers"; tinyactors-cpython/ROADMAP.md, "The API review" (the surface completed against core's headers).

decision.question: May a JavaScript programmer await a typed method?
decision.option: Yes, in the convenience layer: await host.actorState({session}) is a few lines of JavaScript over the direct layer's method, resolving in onResult and rejecting with the TinyactorsError in onError; the direct layer keeps response handlers and returns nothing.
A promise returned by the direct layer's method itself.
decision.recommendation: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): "for JavaScript, the promise makes sense ... it was a problem in the core only for draining correctly and response ordering, but since we're just binding core methods, then the promise-based version is just a convenience layer on what a JavaScript programmer would write anyway." It keeps ADR 0012 decision 3 for the direct layer, where the reply is dispatched by the drain in C and ordered by the takes, and adds a shape, not behaviour (bindings.md section 1): the promise settles from the response handler, its continuation runs as a microtask after the turn's native call returns, outside the drain, on a result already converted, and an input it makes schedules a turn like any other. A reply's error always has a handler then, so none is thrown from the turn.
decision.evidence: docs/adr/0012-lifetimes-follow-the-loop.md:193-206 (decision 3: "Node's shape of the same rule is decided in step 8.5"); tinyactors-core/docs/bindings.md section 1, "Two layers".

findings.refuted-by: a fresh agent, 2026-10-16, against the plan at a69e717, with spikes on node 22.22.0 and 22.23.3 and bun 1.4.2

finding.claim: A detached external ArrayBuffer is not a safe Compiled.image; one copy is.
finding.scenario: An application writes compiled.image to a .tai file with await fs.promises.writeFile and closes the Compiled before the write completes (or calls image.buffer.transfer()); the compile result is freed while the write still reads it.
finding.evidence: tinyactors-core/docs/boundary.md section 7 (the same readers, spiked for host outputs on 2026-10-14).
finding.action: Decision d-image: copy once on first read.
finding.refutation: Confirmed by the refutation (boundary.md section 7); it found p1-compile and AGENTS.md still describing the view, both now changed, and that a read after close should throw TA_ERROR_STALE, as Python's does.

finding.claim: A session scope made with Object.create(null) costs five times the memory in V8 of one made from a shared frozen prototype of null prototype.
finding.scenario: The capacity planner's 10,000 resident actors of a three-variable chart on the native datamodel under node: 280 B against 56 B of scope each.
finding.action: p1-datamodel makes scopes from a per-chart prototype; p1-measure reports the result.
finding.refutation: Plausible: the 56 B held only for four properties with constant getters; with the session's link a scope from Object.create is 96 B, a per-chart constructor 64 B. Settled by p1-measure on the scope as built; the gap is V8's only.

finding.claim: A Host cannot be reached from another environment: posting it to a worker gives a plain clone, which the type tag refuses; recording the environment is a check that cannot fail through the public API.
finding.scenario: An application passes its Host to a worker_threads Worker to send from there.
finding.action: The worker test in p1-rules checks the refusal of the clone; the rulebook's "record it and refuse calls from others" stays as an assertion.
finding.refutation: Confirmed by a rerun under both runtimes.

finding.claim: With the event loop driving every host (d-drive), an error kept for the next idle() would often never surface.
finding.scenario: A server sends to actors from HTTP handlers and never awaits idle(); an I/O processor handler throws; Python's rule keeps the error until an idle() that never comes.
finding.refutation: Confirmed; the refutation added the rejection after the turn, now in d-errors.

finding.claim: The Host's finalizer must free the host with basic-env calls only, and the addon must not use node_api_post_finalizer.
finding.scenario: An application drops a Host without close(); the collector finalizes it; ta_host_free calls destroy and release on the native datamodel, which delete napi_refs.
finding.evidence: s-napi: node_api_post_finalizer is under NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL in Node 22 (js_native_api.h:538-545).
Node-API documentation: napi_delete_reference and napi_adjust_external_memory take node_api_basic_env (Node 22 js_native_api.h).
When Bun runs a NAPI_VERSION 8 finalizer, and which calls it allows there.
finding.action: p1-host: the finalizer path calls ta_host_free with the deferred drops done at once (napi_delete_reference), skips the last take; a test under both runtimes.
finding.refutation: Plausible, for another reason: at NAPI_VERSION 8 both runtimes ran the finalizer after gc() returned, where JS calls worked, and Node 22's node_api_basic_env is a plain napi_env without NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL (js_native_api_types.h:46-54), so nothing enforces basic-only and post_finalizer is irrelevant; basic-only stays the rule for the environment's teardown (Node gave napi_pending_exception there). The real hazard is a finalizer that never runs, a cycle through handlers held by strong refs: now in p1-host.

finding.claim: Materializing a send when its handler returns a thenable covers both async functions and promise-returning functions; detection at registration covers only the first.
finding.scenario: ioProcessors: {http: (host, send) => fetch(send.target, {body: send.data}).then(r => send.answer('http.done'))}: a plain function; its continuation runs after the ack.
finding.refutation: Confirmed; the soundness rules are in d-async.

finding.claim: Each expression is compiled by its own napi_run_script, and a SyntaxError is kept for its evaluation, not raised at chart_attach.
finding.scenario: A chart with one malformed cond: SCXML wants error.execution when it is evaluated (W3C 312's rule for an illegal expression), and the chart's other expressions must still run; one script for the whole chart would fail them all.
finding.evidence: tinyactors-cpython/AGENTS.md, "The "python" datamodel" (reported when evaluated, W3C test 312); datamodel_ecmascript.c compiles per expression (:227-265).
finding.refutation: Confirmed, corrected: quickjs compiles each expression lazily at its first evaluation, not at chart_attach (datamodel_ecmascript.c:222-250); p1-datamodel says so.

finding.claim: The native datamodel cannot find a script's top-level declarations from its engine through Node-API, and quickjs's analysis, linked into the addon anyway, can.
finding.scenario: W3C 452: <script>function testobject() {...}</script> and expr="new testobject();" on the native datamodel.
finding.evidence: datamodel_ecmascript.c:887-933 (throw 0 in a fresh context); tinyactors-napi/mise/napi.rb, CORE_SOURCES (the ECMAScript datamodel is linked).
s-js: pre-declare and copy out works in both engines.
finding.action: Decision d-declarations; request r-declarations once the maintainer agrees.
finding.refutation: Refuted: the engine can be asked (node:vm with quickjs's throw 0 trick), and the names would not help, since copy-out breaks closures and var does not write the scope. Replaced by decision d-declarations (refuse, or isolate at a measured cost); r-declarations withdrawn.

finding.claim: The native datamodel needs B.2's XML DOM, which today exists only as a static string inside quickjs's datamodel.
finding.scenario: W3C 557 and 561 on the native datamodel.
finding.action: Decided: the DOM is built from txml in the addon (d-dom); the native capture copies a DOM value (W3C 561).
finding.refutation: Plausible: today's prelude installs __ta_xml on globalThis, so r-dom asks for a form that installs nothing; the native capture must copy the DOM (W3C 561). Settled when core states the exported form.

finding.claim: The application must be able to choose quickjs for a host, through the public API.
finding.scenario: The suite's quickjs runs go through conform.mjs, which imports only the package (its lint); and an application running charts it does not trust needs max_ops and a bounded heap.
finding.evidence: tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, "Tasks" (the adapter imports only @tinyactors/node); driver.md:72-82; datamodel_ecmascript.h (max_ops, memory_limit).
finding.refutation: Confirmed for the suite (system.c:224-230: the first name match wins); the sandbox reason holds only if the option passes quickjs's limits, which Python does not: now in d-datamodel, with the default left to the maintainer.

finding.claim: The Node rulebook predates ADR 0014 and ADR 0017: it still speaks of envelopes, PEER and synchronous I/O processors.
finding.scenario: A session building from tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md as it stands would design a peer API core no longer has.
finding.evidence: tinyactors-napi/AGENTS.md, "What reaches the application" and "Lifetimes and thin views"; tinyactors-napi/ROADMAP.md, "Done means"; commits d7db9ad, f4c2819.
finding.refutation: Confirmed, and the replacement was already stale: bf0b8a1 removed TA_HOST_TRANSPORT (the transport is io_processor 0) and f53ae02 added messages, host.fail and address parts; c-transport, c-image and c-resolver now say so.

finding.claim: Node needs no attach step before the event loop drives a host.
finding.scenario: A server calls host.send from an HTTP handler and never calls idle(); with Python's rule no turn would run until something drove the host.
finding.action: Decided by the maintainer (2026-10-16): decision d-drive, transparent; no synchronous driver; d-clock follows from it.
finding.refutation: Confirmed; decided by the maintainer. The refutation's costs (a pending deadline keeps a script alive, the timer holds the Host) are in d-drive for the README.

finding.claim: Values that cross between realms fail instanceof: an array from the application, or from a session of another context, is not instanceof Array in a chart's context.
finding.scenario: W3C 457 checks instanceof Array on a foreach collection; an application sends [1, 2] as event data and a chart tests _event.data instanceof Array.
finding.evidence: s-vm: [false, true] for instanceof Array and Array.isArray.
finding.action: Capture and inputs already copy mutable values (actors share no mutable value): make the copy with the receiving context's constructors, so a payload is of the datamodel's shared realm; a session of its own context gets its copy at bind_event. One shared context per host's datamodel (d-declarations) keeps that copy to the isolated charts. Settled by W3C 457 and a test with application data.

finding.claim: The plan's API mirrored Python's, not core's headers: nothing checked that every public function of core is exposed, used internally or left out with a reason.
finding.scenario: A scan of the public headers (2026-10-16) against the plan's api section found core functions an application could want and no row names: address formatting, quickjs's memory limit and last error, BasicHTTP's encoder and parser.
finding.evidence: tinyactors-core/docs/bindings.md section 2 ("inventory the public headers it drives and write the mapping table ... A core function with no item is used internally (say where) or not exposed (say why)"); root AGENTS.md, "Bindings expose the core, nothing else".
finding.action: Step p0-inventory and decision d-layers. Raised by the maintainer (2026-10-16).

spike.question: Do the Node-API calls the plan relies on behave the same in Node.js and Bun?
spike.setup: One C addon (NAPI_VERSION 8) built against the pinned node's headers, loaded by node and bun. First run: clang 18.1.3, node v22.22.0, bun 1.4.2. Rerun on the pins (mise): clang 22.1.8, node v22.23.3, bun 1.4.1, with the same results.
spike.result: Both: napi_type_tag_object and its check; napi_adjust_external_memory; an external ArrayBuffer, and napi_detach_arraybuffer leaving its Uint8Array and byteLength at 0 (detached true); napi_get_value_string_utf8 turns 'a\uD800b' into 61 EF BF BD 62 with no error; napi_get_value_int64 gives 9223372036854775807 for 2**70, 1 for 1.5 and 0 for NaN, all with napi_ok; 1000 wrapped objects finalized after a forced collection (gc() under --expose-gc, Bun.gc(true)); a setTimeout called from C returns an object with ref, unref and hasRef. node_api_post_finalizer is exported by both binaries but declared only under NAPI_EXPERIMENTAL in Node 22's js_native_api.h:538-545.

spike.question: Does quickjs's compiled shape work in V8 and JavaScriptCore through napi_run_script, and do the scoped-form symbols exist?
spike.setup: The same addon's napi_run_script on (function(__s){with(__s){return [function(){'use strict';return (x + 1)}, function(__v){'use strict'; y = __v}, function(){ var z = 5; function f(){return 7} __s.f = f }]}}) with a null-prototype scope. Run on node v22.22.0 and bun 1.4.2, then again on the pins (node v22.23.3, bun 1.4.1) with the same results.
spike.result: Both runtimes: the getter reads the scope (2); assigning an undeclared y throws ReferenceError "y is not defined", and once scope.y exists the assignment writes it; a function copied out with __s.f = f is on the scope; an unknown name falls through to globalThis. Corrected after the refutation (the first script printed undefined fields away and recorded a returned SyntaxError as success): var z = 5 inside the with does NOT write the pre-declared scope.z (undefined on both); a using declaration is a SyntaxError on node v22.22.0 and v22.23.3 and parses on bun. Symbol.dispose and Symbol.asyncDispose are symbols on both.

spike.question: Can an async function be told at registration?
spike.setup: Object.prototype.toString.call(async function(){}) in both runtimes. Run on node v22.22.0 and bun 1.4.2, then again on the pins (node v22.23.3, bun 1.4.1) with the same results.

spike.question: What does a session scope object cost, by how it is made?
spike.setup: 100,000 objects with four properties each (three variables and _event), heap measured after forced collections: process.memoryUsage().heapUsed under node --expose-gc, bun:jsc heapStats().heapSize under bun. Run on node v22.22.0 and bun 1.4.2, then again on the pins (node v22.23.3, bun 1.4.1) with the same results.
spike.result: node v22.22.0: Object.create(null) 280 B per object (V8 makes a null-prototype object a dictionary); Object.create(a shared frozen prototype of null prototype) 56 B; a per-chart constructor 56 B; an object literal 56 B. bun 1.4.2: 64 B for the first three, 48 B for the literal. The refutation's rerun with what a real scope holds: a fifth own property (the session's link the system variables' getters read) takes Object.create's scope to 96 B, a per-chart constructor with the link, three variables and a read-only _event is 64 B; the fivefold gap is V8's only.

spike.question: Can node:vm give the native datamodel a realm of its own per chart or per session, and tell which charts need one, without a parser of ours?
spike.setup: process.getBuiltinModule('node:vm') on node v22.23.3 and bun 1.4.1 (the pins): 50 contexts made and measured; the script var count = 0; function inc(){ count++ } let b = 1; const c = 2; class D {} after throw 0; in a scratch context; a shared context evaluating a session's scope through the with shape; 200 per-session contexts running the script; an application array tested inside a context.
spike.result: A context: 144 KB and 898 µs on node, 54 KB and 397 µs on bun; per session with the script: 143 KB on node, 60 KB on bun. The global's new names after the throw: count and inc on both; b, c and D answer ReferenceError (temporal dead zone). The shared context reads the scope (2); the per-session closure counts to 2; the application's globalThis has no inc. An application array inside the context: instanceof Array false, Array.isArray true.

request.what: A public function of the ECMAScript datamodel's library that gives a script's top-level declarations as quickjs's analysis finds them (var and function names, each function declaration's source, let, const and class names), for a native ECMAScript datamodel without a per-session global object: it pre-declares the names on the scope, copies function and lexical bindings out after the script, and re-creates declared functions on deserialize, as quickjs does for its isolated sessions.
request.why: Decision d-declarations: W3C 452 and charts that define helper functions in a <script>. quickjs asks its engine by evaluating throw 0; before the script in a fresh context and reading the global object's own names (datamodel_ecmascript.c:887-933); Node-API cannot make a fresh realm, and the same trick in the application's realm would hoist the chart's names onto its globalThis.
request.shown-by: Withdrawn after the refutation: pre-declaring and copying out is unsound (closures over the script's vars), so the names alone would not help; decision d-declarations needs nothing of core.

request.what: The XML DOM quickjs uses for B.2 content, exported as text in a form that installs nothing on the global object (a function expression called with the content), so both ECMAScript datamodels build the same DOM.
request.why: Decision d-dom: one DOM for both ECMAScript datamodels.
